recommendation: Keep the source-changing commit as-is. No broader core change is needed for FHIR-32064 because warning structure, terminology, example, narrative, and constraints are already present; this commit closes the remaining stale root-definition omission.
issue_request: FHIR-32064 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for R5. It requested minimal warning support in ClinicalUseIssue/ClinicalUseDefinition by adding a warning backbone with description/code, removing the old generic description element, adding warning to Scope and Boundaries, and constraining use to one of the five issue types.
initial_application: The issue had been substantially applied by Jira-tagged commits 07fb4bd, 62ca66a, c5e2a5b, and f4592866, which added the warning backbone, warning terminology binding, warning narrative text, and removed ClinicalUseDefinition.description. Current source also contains a warning example and later type/backbone invariants, but the root differential element still described only indication, contraindication, interaction, and undesirable effect.
additional_context: FHIR-31847 renamed ClinicalUseIssue to ClinicalUseDefinition before the warning work landed. OO Catalog minutes in August 2021 tracked FHIR-32064 through final discussion and application, including the Scope/Boundaries text that is now present. Zulip discussion supports the warning use case and later shows the warning backbone with description and code. FHIR-48893 later refined ClinicalUseDefinition invariants and confirms warning remains one of the five type-specific backbones.
reconciliation: Updated source/clinicalusedefinition/structuredefinition-ClinicalUseDefinition.xml so the ClinicalUseDefinition root element short and definition include warning alongside indication, contraindication, interaction, and undesirable effect.
source_changes: source/clinicalusedefinition/structuredefinition-ClinicalUseDefinition.xml: updated the ClinicalUseDefinition root element short and definition to include warning as a supported issue type.
